title: Settings
description: How Portta names projects, who can reach them, and how this panel is reached.
saved: Saved. Traefik reads its static configuration at startup, so these values take effect once the gateway containers are recreated on the host:
notWritable: The panel cannot write {{path}}. Edit it on the host instead.
chooseGroup: Choose one of the available groups.
secretsNote: Secrets are never returned by the API: the panel only reports whether a token is set. Values are written to {{path}} with mode 600.
restartPending: These changes take effect after the gateway is recreated. Save now, then use the apply bar.

dashboard.title: Traefik dashboard
dashboard.description: The address this host is serving right now. Apply saved settings from the bar at the bottom.
dashboard.loopbackHint: This loopback address only works on this machine. The dashboard has no login of its own, so it is never published on a domain.
dashboard.tailnetWarning: On a Tailscale attachment, :8080 is also reachable on the tailnet with no login while the loopback overlay is active.
dashboard.openDisabled: No usable address from here. The loopback URL only works on the host.

projectDomain.title: Resulting addresses
projectDomain.description: Portta builds each project hostname from this base.
projectDomain.examples: A project called loja would answer on:
projectDomain.note: This chooses the name only. Who can reach Traefik is decided under Project access.

panel.networkHelp: The host port and interface used to publish the panel. These are separate from the browser URL; routed modes derive and lock the bind.

kinds.public: On the panel port, from the internet

kindHelp.local: http://127.0.0.1 and the port above. The default, and the safest.
kindHelp.tailscale: Bind the panel to this node’s tailnet address. Sign-in becomes required.
kindHelp.public: Publish the panel on its own port. Does not publish your projects. Sign-in becomes required.
kindHelp.hostname: Reach the panel at a name. Sign-in becomes required. Projects stay as they are.

panel.subdomainHelp: Only the label. The base comes from the project addresses already configured.
panel.customDomainHelp: This name must resolve to this server. Configure DNS and TLS if they are not already set.
panel.publicAddressHelp: The IP address or hostname people type before the panel port. The protocol and port are added automatically.
panel.publicAddressNeeded: Enter an address reachable from the internet so Portta can build the sign-in URL.
panel.authRequired: The panel will ask people to sign in. Changing this does not publish your projects.
panel.tlsNeeded: A hostname on HTTPS needs TLS to be enabled. docs/addresses-and-access.md#tls
panel.tailnetBindNeeded: Enter this node's Tailscale address under Panel network before saving.
panel.securityHelp: Who may use the panel, and from which origins.

projectAccess.title: Who can reach projects

kindHelp.local: Traefik listens only on 127.0.0.1. This is the safest default.
kindHelp.private: Traefik joins the Tailscale tailnet; public access stays off.
kindHelp.public: Publishes HTTP and HTTPS on every interface. Only services that opted into routing answer.

projectAccess.vpnHelp: Choose a Portta-managed tailnet or bind an existing VPN interface. A private domain may override the project base.

privateKinds.interface: VPN already installed on this host

privateKindHelp.tailscale: The self-contained default. Traefik joins the Tailscale container's network.
privateKindHelp.interface: Bind Traefik to the private address of a host-native Tailscale or another VPN.

projectAccess.privateBindNeeded: Enter the private address of this host's VPN interface. Portta will still refuse 0.0.0.0.
projectAccess.privateDomainNeeded: localhost resolves to each person's own machine. Choose automatic project addresses or enter a private domain that resolves to this server.
projectAccess.customDomainHelp: A wildcard record for this domain must point to this server.
projectAccess.needsDomain: localhost cannot work over the internet. Configure automatic addresses or your own domain, or enter another public domain.
projectAccess.noTls: Traffic will use unencrypted HTTP. Configure TLS before using this access in production.
projectAccess.networkHelp: Traefik ports and logs. The bind address is derived from the access mode above.
projectAccess.confirmTitle: Make projects reachable from the internet?
projectAccess.confirmDescription: This change recreates the gateway in a configuration reachable from public networks.
projectAccess.confirmWarning: The panel, datastores, and unrouted services remain outside this access. Routed projects without protection may be reached by anyone.

publicAccess.needsDomain: localhost is not reachable from the internet. Set a public project domain, or switch project addresses to automatic or your own domain first.
publicAccess.result: Opted-in projects will be reachable as <project>-<service>.{{domain}}.
publicAccess.tlsOff: Traffic would be plaintext. Enable TLS before leaving this on. docs/addresses-and-access.md#tls

groupIntro.Projects: The directory this installation treats as home for Projects.
groupIntro.Project domain: How Portta names projects and services. A name is not an exposure.
groupIntro.Gateway: Where Traefik listens. Independent of the panel address.
groupIntro.Project access: Where Traefik listens and whether projects answer only here, over the VPN, or on the internet. This does not publish the panel.
groupIntro.Public access: Whether the internet can reach Traefik. It does not change how projects are named, and it does not publish this panel.
groupIntro.VPN: Reach projects on a tailnet instead of the public network.
groupIntro.TLS: Certificates for project hostnames. Not assumed just because a domain is set.
groupIntro.DNS: Optional Cloudflare automation for the wildcard record and DNS-01. It does not choose the project domain.
groupIntro.Panel: How you reach this panel. Independent of whether projects are public.
groupIntro.Traefik: The reverse proxy that routes every hostname. Its unauthenticated dashboard stays on loopback, except when Traefik shares the Tailscale namespace.

ACME_CA_SERVER.label: ACME directory
ACME_CA_SERVER.help: Point at the staging endpoint while testing to avoid rate limits.

ACME_CHALLENGE.label: How to prove the domain
ACME_CHALLENGE.help: DNS issues one wildcard and needs a provider credential. HTTP issues one certificate per hostname and needs port 80 reachable from the internet.

ACME_DNS_PROVIDER.label: DNS-01 provider
ACME_DNS_PROVIDER.help: Provider name as understood by Traefik/lego. Needed when the challenge is DNS.

ACME_EMAIL.label: Let’s Encrypt contact
ACME_EMAIL.help: Required when certificates come from Let’s Encrypt.

CF_DNS_API_TOKEN.label: Cloudflare API token
CF_DNS_API_TOKEN.help: A scoped token (Zone:DNS:Edit), never the global API key.

CLOUDFLARE_ENABLED.label: Cloudflare DNS
CLOUDFLARE_ENABLED.help: Create the wildcard record and answer DNS-01 challenges through Cloudflare. This does not choose the project domain.

CLOUDFLARE_ZONE.label: Cloudflare zone
CLOUDFLARE_ZONE.help: The zone the wildcard record lives in.

GITHUB_API_URL.label: API base URL
GITHUB_API_URL.help: https://api.github.com, or your GitHub Enterprise Server API root.

GITHUB_APP_ENABLED.label: GitHub App
GITHUB_APP_ENABLED.help: Off by default. With this off the panel makes no outbound request and behaves exactly as before.

GITHUB_APP_ID.label: App id
GITHUB_APP_ID.help: The numeric id GitHub shows on the App settings page. Not a secret.

GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE.label: Private key file
GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE.help: The .pem inside the container. The directory is fixed by the mount; the filename is the one GitHub gave you. Read-only at mode 600, and never a .env value.

GITHUB_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET.label: Webhook secret
GITHUB_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET.help: Verifies deliveries GitHub sends. Stored as a secret and never returned.

PORTTA_ACCESS_LOG.label: Traefik access log
PORTTA_ACCESS_LOG.help: Useful while debugging routing, noisy otherwise.

PORTTA_AUTH_MODE.label: Authentication
PORTTA_AUTH_MODE.help: Required makes the panel ask who you are. Disabled makes every request the local operator, and is only allowed on this machine.

PORTTA_AUTH_SECRET.label: Session signing secret
PORTTA_AUTH_SECRET.help: What sessions and tokens are signed with. Generated during bootstrap; rotating it signs everybody out.

PORTTA_AUTO_DOMAIN_PROVIDER.label: Automatic DNS service
PORTTA_AUTO_DOMAIN_PROVIDER.help: sslip.io and nip.io both resolve any name that embeds this host address, so neither needs a record or an account.

PORTTA_BIND_ADDRESS.label: Listen on
PORTTA_BIND_ADDRESS.help: Interface Traefik publishes on. 127.0.0.1 keeps project traffic off the local network.

PORTTA_DASHBOARD.label: Traefik dashboard
PORTTA_DASHBOARD.help: Traefik's own dashboard. It stays on loopback normally; a Tailscale attachment can also make it reachable on the tailnet without login.

PORTTA_DASHBOARD_ADVERTISED_HOST.label: Dashboard hostname
PORTTA_DASHBOARD_ADVERTISED_HOST.help: Derived as <project>-traefik.<domain> unless you override it.

PORTTA_DASHBOARD_EXPOSE.label: Dashboard access
PORTTA_DASHBOARD_EXPOSE.help: The dashboard stays on loopback. It has no credential of its own, so it is never routed on a domain.

choices.domain: Legacy domain routing — change to local

PORTTA_DASHBOARD_PORT.label: Dashboard port
PORTTA_DASHBOARD_PORT.help: Host port for the Traefik dashboard.

PORTTA_DOMAIN.label: Your domain
PORTTA_DOMAIN.help: The base Portta uses to build project addresses. A wildcard *.<domain> must resolve to this host.

PORTTA_DOMAIN_MODE.label: How addresses are built
PORTTA_DOMAIN_MODE.help: This machine uses localhost. Automatic builds a name from this host address, with no DNS record. Your own domain needs a wildcard pointing here.

PORTTA_LOG_LEVEL.label: Log level
PORTTA_LOG_LEVEL.help: Log level for the gateway components.

PORTTA_PANEL_TRUSTED_ORIGINS.label: Extra trusted origins
PORTTA_PANEL_TRUSTED_ORIGINS.help: Other origins a browser may sign in from, comma-separated: a VPN name, a public domain. Loopback and the panel URL are always trusted.

PORTTA_PANEL_URL.label: Panel URL
PORTTA_PANEL_URL.help: The address a browser reaches the panel on. It decides where sign-in redirects to, and whether the session cookie may be `Secure`.

PORTTA_PROFILE.label: Gateway profile
PORTTA_PROFILE.help: Where Traefik listens: this machine, a private network, or the internet. Independent of the panel.

PORTTA_PROJECTS_HOME.label: Projects Home
PORTTA_PROJECTS_HOME.help: The one directory this installation manages Projects in. Changing it changes the reference; files are not moved. Existing environments outside this path stay visible as unmanaged.

PORTTA_PUBLIC_IP.label: Host address
PORTTA_PUBLIC_IP.help: The IPv4 address automatic mode embeds in the hostname. Detected during installation.

PORTTA_RUNTIME_API_DOCS.label: API reference
PORTTA_RUNTIME_API_DOCS.help: Serve the API reference and its console at /docs/api. It issues real requests against this panel, so empty uses the safe default: on for loopback, off when routed.

PORTTA_RUNTIME_DB_PASSWORD.label: Database password
PORTTA_RUNTIME_DB_PASSWORD.help: Generated bootstrap credential for the panel-owned PostgreSQL database.

PORTTA_RUNTIME_DOCS.label: Documentation
PORTTA_RUNTIME_DOCS.help: Serve the project's documentation at /docs, from this image. Static text with no host information in it, so a routed panel may serve it.

PORTTA_WEB_BIND_ADDRESS.label: Bind
PORTTA_WEB_BIND_ADDRESS.help: Host interface used to publish the panel. Keep 127.0.0.1 unless it is a tailnet address or you explicitly enable the public entrypoint.

PORTTA_WEB_EXPOSE.label: How the panel is reached
PORTTA_WEB_EXPOSE.help: This machine is loopback only. The other modes put the panel beyond this host and require sign-in. None of them publishes your projects.

PORTTA_WEB_HOST.label: Panel subdomain
PORTTA_WEB_HOST.help: The label in front of the project domain when the panel is reached as a subdomain.

PORTTA_PANEL_ADVERTISED_HOST.label: Panel hostname
PORTTA_PANEL_ADVERTISED_HOST.help: The hostname Traefik routes to the panel when it is reached by a domain.

PORTTA_WEB_PORT.label: Port
PORTTA_WEB_PORT.help: Host port used to publish the panel.

PORTTA_WEB_READ_ONLY.label: Read-only
PORTTA_WEB_READ_ONLY.help: Refuse every mutating endpoint. The default whenever the panel is routed.

PRIVATE_DOMAIN.label: Private domain
PRIVATE_DOMAIN.help: Optional wildcard served only over the VPN. Leave empty to reuse the project domain base.

PUBLIC_DOMAIN.label: Public project domain
PUBLIC_DOMAIN.help: Domain used to publish opted-in projects on the internet, for example dev.example.com. A wildcard must point at this host.

PUBLIC_ENABLED.label: Internet access
PUBLIC_ENABLED.help: Lets the internet reach Traefik on ports 80 and 443. It does not change how projects are named, and it does not publish the panel. Only services that opt in are routed.

TAILSCALE_ENABLED.label: Tailscale
TAILSCALE_ENABLED.help: Run Traefik inside the Tailscale network namespace so projects are reachable on the tailnet, not the public NIC.

TAILSCALE_HOSTNAME.label: Tailscale hostname
TAILSCALE_HOSTNAME.help: Name this node takes on the tailnet.

TLS_ENABLED.label: HTTPS
TLS_ENABLED.help: Issue certificates for project hostnames. Off, only HTTP is served.

TLS_MODE.label: Certificate source
TLS_MODE.help: This machine uses a local CA. Let’s Encrypt uses ACME.

GITHUB_SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES.label: Reconciliation interval
GITHUB_SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES.help: Minutes between passes that re-read what changed. A loopback panel cannot receive webhooks, so this is what keeps the projection fresh. 0 turns it off.

TS_AUTHKEY.label: Tailscale auth key
TS_AUTHKEY.help: Prefer an ephemeral, tagged, pre-authorised key. Never leaves the host.

validation.mustBeHostname: must be a hostname, for example dev.example.com
validation.mustBePort: must be a port between 1 and 65535
validation.mustBeUsername: must be 1 to 64 characters of letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore
validation.mustBePasswordHash: must be an apr1, bcrypt or SHA1 hash; run: portta web auth set
validation.mustBeNumericAppId: must be the numeric App id
validation.mustBeUnderGithubKeyDir: must be under /app/state/github/, the directory mounted into the panel
validation.notManaged: is not a setting the panel manages
validation.publicDomainRequired: is required by the remote-public profile
validation.bindAddressPrivate: the remote-private profile must not bind 0.0.0.0
validation.acmeEmailRequired: is required when TLS_MODE is acme
validation.tailscaleHostnameRequired: is required when Tailscale is enabled
validation.authBasicRequired: must be basic while the panel is routed
validation.credentialRequired: a routed panel needs a credential: run portta web auth set
validation.panelNotOnEveryInterface: the panel is not published on every interface; reach it over the VPN instead

restartHint: Changing this takes effect after the gateway restarts, not when it is saved.
pendingHint: Saved, but the running process still has {{value}}.

roleHints.owner: Owns this panel. There is exactly one, and the role moves by transfer.
roleHints.admin: Everything except taking ownership. Sees every Project.
roleHints.developer: Works on the Projects they are a member of: tasks, environments, repositories.
roleHints.viewer: Reads the Projects they are a member of, and changes nothing.

localMode.title: This panel does not sign people in
localMode.users: It runs in local mode: it answers on loopback, where reaching it already means having the machine. There are no accounts to manage. Set PORTTA_AUTH_MODE=protected on the host to turn accounts on.
localMode.tokens: A token belongs to a person, and this panel has none. Set PORTTA_AUTH_MODE=protected on the host to turn accounts and tokens on.
localMode.security: There is no account to secure: this panel answers on loopback without asking who is asking. Set PORTTA_AUTH_MODE=protected on the host to turn accounts on.
localMode.audit: The audit log records who did what, and here everybody is the local operator. Set PORTTA_AUTH_MODE=protected on the host to turn accounts on.

agentPermissions.title: What a local agent may do
agentPermissions.description: The ceiling over a request that announces itself with X-Portta-Actor. It narrows what the person behind it holds; it never grants anything extra.

users.title: Users
users.description: Who can sign in, what each of them may do, and which Projects they reach.
users.createDescription: The account exists as soon as you create it. Hand over the first password yourself: this panel sends no email.
users.name: Name
users.passwordSignsOut: Changing a password signs that account out of every other browser.
users.noProjectsYet: This panel has no Projects yet.
users.projectAccessHint: A developer or a viewer sees the Projects they are a member of, and nothing else.
users.sessionsDescription: The browsers this account is signed in on right now.
users.noSessions: This account is not signed in anywhere.
users.transferImpact: {{name}} becomes the owner and you become an administrator, in one step. There is no way back except asking them to transfer it again.
users.banImpact: The account stops working on its next request. Nothing is deleted, and the ban can be lifted.
users.removeImpact: The account, its sessions and its tokens are deleted. What the account did stays in the audit log.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: Credentials for what is not a browser: the CLI on a laptop, an agent in a terminal, a job in CI.
tokens.createDescription: A token can never do more than your role does. Lowering your role lowers every token you made.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.nameHint: What this credential is for: the laptop, the CI job, the agent.

actorHint.agent: Narrowed further by what agents may do on this panel.
actorHint.human: Holds what your role holds, as if it were you at the keyboard.

tokens.expiresHint: A credential with no end is one nobody remembers to end.
tokens.scopeNote: The token holds the intersection of its scopes and your role, computed on every request.
tokens.revokeImpact: Whatever carries this token stops working on its next request. The row stays, so the listing can still say what was revoked.
tokens.emptyHint: Create one to sign in from the CLI or to let an agent act on your behalf.
tokens.createdDescription: Copy it now: the panel keeps a hash, not the secret.
tokens.onlyOnce: This is the only time this secret is shown. If it is lost, revoke this token and make another.
tokens.useHint: Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>, or run portta auth login and paste it.

security.title: Security
security.description: Your own account: your password, your second factor, and where you are signed in.
security.passwordDescription: There is no reset by email. An administrator sets a new one, or you run portta auth reset-password on the host.
security.changePasswordDescription: You will stay signed in here, and be signed out everywhere else.
security.twoFactorDescription: An authenticator app, asked for after your password.
security.twoFactorHint: Turning it on adds one step to your sign-in and nothing else. Backup codes are shown once, when you turn it on.
security.confirmPassword: Your password, to be sure it is you.
security.scanDescription: Then type the six-digit code it shows, so the panel knows the app works.
security.qrLabel: QR code for your authenticator app
security.cannotScan: If the app cannot scan, type this secret instead:
security.invalidCode: That code was not accepted. Codes change every 30 seconds.
security.backupDescription: Each works once, in place of a code from the app.
security.backupOnce: This is the only time they are shown. Keep them somewhere you can reach without this panel.
security.sessionsDescription: Every browser holding a session for this account.
security.sessionsRefused: The panel would not answer about your sessions.
security.totpUnavailable: This panel could not turn on an authenticator app.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.description: What the panel talks to that is not the host.

audit.title: Audit
audit.description: Who did what: accounts, roles, tokens, Project membership and settings. Development activity lives on the Activity page.
audit.emptyHint: Entries appear as accounts, tokens and settings are changed.
